The weather systems that are expected to affect the country during Holy Week or Semana Santa are the Easterlies and the Ridge of High Pressure Area (HPA).

The public is advised to avoid physical outdoor activities between 10:00 in the morning and 4:00 in the afternoon. 

To avoid fatigue, heat cramps, and heat exhaustion:

text:
Alamin kung paano umiral at nakaapekto sa bansa ang Habagat noong 2025. ☔️

The DOST-PAGASA presents the 2025 Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) Assessment (ISSN: 3116-4811), providing an overview and analysis of how last year’s Habagat season developed and progressed across the Philippines.

In his message, the DOST-PAGASA Administrator, Dr. Nathaniel T. Servando, stated: 
"The publication of the 2025 Philippine Southwest Monsoon Assessment provides a comprehensive account of the evolution and impacts of the Southwest Monsoon (SWM) in the Philippines. I am pleased to present this technical report, which highlights the results of DOST-PAGASA’s operational monitoring efforts and the continued advancement of monsoon research in the country."

🎯What’s inside the report:
• Onset and withdrawal of the Habagat
• Periods of enhanced monsoon activity
• Influence of tropical cyclones
• Rainfall patterns and notable events

💡Key highlights:
• Onset in early June and withdrawal in early October
• Generally strong monsoon conditions
• Nine (9) tropical cyclones enhanced the Habagat
• Heavier rainfall over Western Luzon and Visayas

Prepared under the MonsoonWatch-PH Project, led by Dr. Joseph Q. Basconcillo and supported by the DOST PCIEERD, this assessment contributes to ongoing efforts to improve the monitoring and understanding of monsoons in the country.

📊 Access the full report here: http://bit.ly/40ETGTy

A three-day refresher course on sustaining & evolving flash flood warning services in the South Asia-Oceania region was conducted last March 26-28. The training was held in a hybrid format to accommodate both in-person and online participants. Experts from India and Fiji served as trainers. On the afternoon of Day 1, participants visited the PAGASA Weather and Flood Forecasting Center in Quezon City as part of the program.

These activities helped strengthen a standardized decision-making tool while enhancing early warning systems and disaster resilience among member states. These efforts support public safety and well-being, and contribute to sustainable development amid the increasing challenges of urbanization, population growth, more frequent extreme weather events, and climate change.

DOST-PAGASA hosted this year’s 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗵 𝗔𝘀𝗶𝗮-𝗢𝗰𝗲𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗮 𝗙𝗹𝗮𝘀𝗵 𝗙𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 (𝗦𝗔𝗢𝗙𝗙𝗚𝗦) Steering Committee Meeting attended by key representatives from the region last March 25 at Lanson Place, Mall of Asia in Pasay City Metro Manila. With full funding from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United States Department of State (USDOS).

This undertaking emphasizes the importance of regional cooperation in safeguarding the region from the impacts of flash floods. This one-day event also serves as a platform for knowledge exchange, capacity strengthening, collaborative planning and revitalizing linkages among national and regional experts. Participants are expected to share their experiences, technical initiatives, and lessons learned in disaster risk reduction and early warning system implementation, particularly on hydrometeorological extreme events. 

The Steering Committee, through this engagement, also aims to chart a sustainable and forward-looking path for improving early warning mechanisms beyond 2026. Through strengthened partnerships and a shared commitment, the body seeks to advance more effective, timely, and inclusive early warning systems across the region.

DOST-PAGASA decommissions seven tropical cyclone names from the 2025 season
 
DOST-PAGASA officially announces the decommissioning of domestic tropical cyclone names CRISING, EMONG, MIRASOL, NANDO, OPONG, TINO, and UWAN from its regular roster due to the significant devastation they caused in 2025. 
 
With the decommissioning of these names, PAGASA will be using the replacement names CHICO, ELIAS, MAGYAWAN, NILAD, OMAR, TALA, and URBANO beginning in 2029.

https://www.pagasa.dost.gov.ph/press-release/203
